clue.text: Still cold wearing tartan

indicators.note: the tartan has the cold letter on it, wrapped around it like a garment

parts.note: plaid is a tartan cloth
C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone stands motionless and chilly while dressed in tartan.
explanation.definitionFit: Placid and still both describe calm water or a calm temperament, so they are synonyms as adjectives.

clue.text: Puts up with depression sending son to the south

indicators.note: together with the later phrase, the son letter is sent elsewhere
in a down entry the south is the bottom, so the letter goes to the end

parts.note: a slump is an economic depression

explanation.surface: Someone endures a low point that drives a son to head south.
explanation.definitionFit: To lump it is an informal idiom for putting up with something unpleasant.

clue.text: Reference sees head replaced by company complicity

indicators.note: the first letter of the reference word gives way to the company letters

parts.note: an allusion is an indirect reference

explanation.surface: A citation shows that a boss was ousted by a firm in a conspiracy.
explanation.definitionFit: Collusion is secret cooperation to cheat or deceive, the same as complicity in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Cover charge in case of disappearance

indicators.note: the charge goes inside the case made by the outer letters
the outer letters of disappearance form a case round the charge

parts.note: a rap is a criminal charge, as in 'take the rap'

explanation.surface: An insurance premium protects against something going missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of' takes D and E, the outside letters of 'disappearance', which wrap around RAP.
explanation.definitionFit: To drape something is to cover it loosely with cloth.

clue.text: Stiffener offered by celebrity before church

indicators.note: the celebrity comes ahead of the church in the finished word

parts.note: a star is a celebrity

explanation.surface: A famous person, on the way to a service, offers something to stiffen a collar.
explanation.definitionFit: Starch is the substance used to stiffen shirts and collars in laundering, so it is literally a stiffener.

clue.text: View taking in shop window

indicators.note: the view word takes the shop inside itself

parts.note: a sight is a view
a deli is a delicatessen shop

explanation.surface: A sight-seer pauses to look in a shop's display window.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidelight is a narrow window beside a door or larger window.

clue.text: A smile across the length of ship

parts.note: a beam is a broad smile

explanation.surface: A grin spreads across the face of a ship's crew from end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: Abeam is a nautical term for at right angles to a vessel's keel, across its length.

clue.text: Country Castro and CIA transformed

indicators.note: the letters of Castro and CIA are changed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The Cuban leader and American spies remake a Central American nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Costa Rica is a nation in Central America, an example of a country.

clue.text: Second refill — don't go to bed yet!

parts.note: a top-up is a refill of a glass

explanation.surface: A host offers another glass and urges the guest to stay up late.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop up is to remain awake past one's usual bedtime, a British informal phrase.

clue.text: Live with desire to fit in

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
to long is to desire

explanation.surface: Someone lives with a yearning to be accepted socially.
explanation.definitionFit: To belong is to feel at home or be accepted in a group, which is to fit in.

clue.text: Spent a million absorbing language

indicators.note: the words Spent a million soak up and hold the answer inside their run of letters

explanation.surface: Someone has blown a million pounds while getting absorbed in learning a language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absorbing' signals the answer is held within 'speNT A MILlion'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamil is a Dravidian tongue spoken in southern India and Sri Lanka, an example of a language.

clue.text: Intended receiver may see a daughter shift ecstasy repeatedly

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter in genealogies
a shift is a simple loose dress

indicators.note: the ecstasy letter is used twice over, one copy after another

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A recipient might watch a daughter take her drug-fuelled shifting dance over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shift' looks like a verb meaning move, but here it is the noun, a loose dress.
explanation.definitionFit: The person a letter or parcel is meant for is the one whose name and address it bears.

clue.text: Opinion of meadow, having love for area

indicators.note: having the love letter in place of the area letter, one swapped for the other

parts.note: pasture is grassy meadow land for grazing
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a view on a field, then rhapsodises about the region.
explanation.definitionFit: A posture can mean a stance or attitude taken on an issue, hence an opinion.

clue.text: Left university doctor with earlier condition …

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
ago means before now, earlier

explanation.surface: A doctor who has quit the university turns out to have had a medical problem before.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to the next clue's surface but plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumbago is lower back pain, a medical complaint or ailment.

clue.text: … as long as offering a supply

definitions.meaning: a conjunction meaning on condition that

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue: the condition holds only if there is something supplied.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works both as a conjunction meaning on condition that and as the participle of supply.

clue.text: Unpopular comedic pieces about Republican fringes

parts.note: out means no longer in fashion, unpopular

indicators.note: the comic pieces go around the Republican letter

parts.note: skits are short comic sketches

explanation.surface: Lame comedy sketches about a Republican come from the political fringe.
explanation.definitionFit: The outskirts are the edges of a town, its outer fringes.

clue.text: Frank is clever, dropping second of internationals for United

indicators.note: with the later word for, this lets one letter fall out and another take its place
puts the United letter in the place of the dropped one

parts.note: ingenious means clever
I is the abbreviation for international; it is the second I of the clever word that goes
U is the abbreviation for United, as in football team names

explanation.surface: An honest player is clever but leaves the international side for United.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the second I of INGENIOUS is swapped for U.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingenuous means innocently open and candid, so it is a synonym of frank.

clue.text: There's no airs, oddly, in looking smart

indicators.note: says the following letters are absent from the gazing word

parts.note: staring is looking hard

indicators.note: takes the first and third letters of the word airs

explanation.surface: A modest person, without pretensions, is nonetheless looking well dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' picks A and R from 'airs'; 'There's no' takes them out of STARING.
explanation.definitionFit: To sting and to smart both mean to feel a sharp burning pain, so they are verb synonyms.

clue.text: Actress troubled about European Union cuts made by these

indicators.note: the jumbled actress letters go around the union letters
the letters of actress are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A disturbed actress complains about budget cuts imposed by the EU.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the whole clue: 'cuts made by these' points to the pruning tool; the anagram from 'troubled' is SECATRS.
explanation.definitionFit: Secateurs are pruning shears, the tool gardeners use to make cuts.

clue.text: Attack messages from the east

indicators.note: in an across entry, reading from the east means running right to left

parts.note: notes are short written messages

explanation.surface: An assault is signalled by dispatches from eastern lands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the east' turns NOTES round to read right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: To set on someone is a phrasal verb meaning to assault or set upon them.

clue.text: Schism underpinning quiet confession

indicators.note: in a down entry the schism sits beneath the quiet letters, supporting them

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
a rift is a split or schism

explanation.surface: A church split lies behind a hushed admission.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrift is an old word for confession to a priest, as in short shrift.

clue.text: Charge sat awkwardly — go in uninvited

indicators.note: the letters of charge and sat are placed clumsily into a new order

explanation.surface: A clumsily seated charge enters a party without being asked.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn up at a party or event without an invitation is the meaning of the verb.

clue.text: Hard borders? Avoids making a decision

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
edges are borders

explanation.surface: A question about firm frontiers, answered by someone sitting on the fence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard borders' looks like the definition, a political phrase, but it is the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To hedge is to avoid committing oneself, as when hedging one's bets.

clue.text: Makes a pile from garden tools at home

parts.note: rakes are toothed garden tools
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone earns a fortune from garden implements without leaving the house.
explanation.definitionFit: To rake it in is an idiom for earning lots of money; making a pile is slang for the same.

clue.text: Colour seen in half of pigs, in the main

indicators.note: puts the half-word inside the sea

parts.note: the main is a poetic term for the open sea

indicators.note: takes the first two of the four letters of pigs

explanation.surface: A shade spotted on some pigs swimming in the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is the old poetic word for the open ocean, as in the Spanish Main.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepia is a reddish-brown shade, from cuttlefish ink, used for old photographs.

clue.text: Wild child's last, behind mad aunt and me

indicators.note: the child's final letter goes after the jumble
crazy signals that the letters of aunt are jumbled
takes the final letter of the word child

explanation.surface: A tearaway youngster trails behind a crazy aunt and the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild child' reads as one phrase, but 'child's last' supplies only D; 'mad' gives UNTA.
explanation.definitionFit: Untamed means not domesticated, a direct synonym of wild.

clue.text: Female employed by small task force not meeting required standards

indicators.note: the female letter is taken on inside the task force

parts.note: a unit is a small military group with a task

explanation.surface: A woman recruited into a small squad fails to make the grade.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfit means not good enough or not up to standard.

clue.text: State of article found in pit

indicators.note: the article is located inside the pit

parts.note: a mine is a pit
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: The condition of an item discovered down a mine.
explanation.definitionFit: Maine is one of the United States, in New England.

clue.text: Provide safety feature seeing Formula One getting blame

parts.note: Formula One motor racing is written F1, with the figure 1 read as the letter I
a reproof is a rebuke or blame

explanation.surface: Motor racing gets criticism, so it must install some safety equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to make something resistant to flames, a safety measure.

clue.text: Come together in backing retinue

indicators.note: the hidden run is read backwards, going in reverse
the letters sit inside the word retinue

explanation.surface: Followers rally together to support a royal entourage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' takes ETINU from inside 'retinue'; 'backing' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: To unite is to join or combine, which is coming together.

clue.text: Analyses for purity when eating second perhaps

indicators.note: the outer word swallows the following pieces into its middle

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'
say means perhaps or for example

explanation.surface: A metallurgist tests samples while having a quick bite.
explanation.definitionFit: To assay a metal or ore is to test its composition, especially its purity.

clue.text: Subject of examination

parts.note: reads like a school subject on an exam paper, but means the person being tested

explanation.definitionFit: A person who is tested or examined is the subject of the test.
